walkthroughs.body_html:
Economic Activity & Energy — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Economic Activity & Energy brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Economic Activity & Energy.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Why is a food web a better model than a food chain?
options: A food web shows what spiders eat and a food chain shows what other animals eat.
A food chain shows one linear path; a food web shows the many interconnected feeding relationships in reality, so it better represents how species depend on multiple food sources.
Qualitative data means high-quality data and quantitative means a lot of data.
A food web is the same as a food chain, just drawn differently.

mcqs.q: Why does the tropical rainforest have distinct vertical layers?
options: Rainforest layers exist because trees grow in age order tallest to shortest.
Rainforest layers exist because different animals live at different heights.
Qualitative data means high-quality data and quantitative means a lot of data.
Competition for light: emergents (40m+), canopy (capturing most light), understorey (shade-tolerant) and forest floor (sparse vegetation due to low light) — each adapted to its light level.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between qualitative and quantitative data?
options: Quantitative data is always more scientific and reliable than qualitative.
A food web shows what spiders eat and a food chain shows what other animals eat.
Qualitative data means high-quality data and quantitative means a lot of data.
Quantitative data is numerical and measurable (traffic counts, river width); qualitative data is descriptive and non-numerical (interview quotes, photo descriptions, field sketches).
